title: When will I receive my payout?
body: Payouts are sent to your bank account on a rolling schedule. Most accounts receive funds two business days after a charge settles. Your first payout can take seven to fourteen days while we verify your business.

title: Why was my payout delayed?
body: A payout can be delayed by a bank holiday, a change to your bank details, or a review of unusual activity. Delayed payouts show a pending status in the dashboard with the expected arrival date.

title: Change the bank account for payouts
body: You can replace the bank account that receives payouts from your settings. For security, changing bank details pauses payouts for up to three days and sends a confirmation email.

title: Instant payouts to a debit card
body: Eligible accounts can send funds to a debit card within minutes for a small fee. Instant payouts are limited by a daily maximum and are not available for every card.

title: Responding to a dispute
body: When a customer disputes a charge with their bank, you can submit evidence such as receipts, shipping tracking and customer messages. Evidence must be submitted before the deadline shown on the dispute.

title: Dispute fees and when they are refunded
body: A dispute fee is charged when a dispute is opened. The fee is returned if the dispute is decided in your favor by the card network.

title: Preventing fraudulent charges
body: Fraud rules let you block payments that match risky patterns, such as many attempts from one card or a mismatch between billing and shipping country. Review blocked payments from the dashboard.

title: Why was a payment declined?
body: Payments are declined by the customer's bank for reasons such as insufficient funds, an incorrect card number or a suspected fraud flag. The decline code in the payment details explains the reason.

title: Accepting payments in another currency
body: You can present prices in more than one hundred currencies. Charges in another currency are converted to your settlement currency at the current exchange rate, and a conversion fee may apply.

title: Saving a card for future payments
body: With the customer's permission you can save a card and charge it later, for example for subscriptions or orders that ship in parts. Saved cards may need authentication on first use.

title: Authorize now and capture later
body: An authorization places a hold on the customer's card without moving money. You can capture the full amount or less within seven days, after which the hold expires.

title: Refunding a customer
body: You can refund all or part of a payment from the payment details page. Refunds usually reach the customer within five to ten business days, depending on their bank.

title: Why did a refund fail?
body: A refund can fail if the customer's card was closed or if your balance is too low to cover it. Failed refunds are listed with the reason so you can send the money another way.

title: Understanding processing fees
body: A processing fee is charged on each successful card payment. International cards and currency conversion can add further fees, and the full breakdown appears in each balance transaction.

title: Downloading invoices and tax documents
body: Monthly fee invoices and annual tax forms are available in the documents section of your settings. Tax forms are issued in January for the previous year.

title: Verifying your business identity
body: To keep payouts enabled, we need details such as your legal business name, tax id and a representative's identity. Missing information is listed in the dashboard with a due date.

title: Adding team members and roles
body: You can invite teammates and give each person a role, such as administrator, developer or support specialist, which controls what they can see and change.

title: Turning on two-step authentication
body: Two-step authentication adds a code from your phone or a security key when you sign in. Administrators can require it for everyone on the team.

title: Closing your account
body: You can close your account once your balance is paid out and there are no open disputes. Closing is permanent, but your records remain available to download for seven years.

title: Changing a customer's subscription plan
body: When a customer upgrades or downgrades, the price difference is prorated by default so they pay only for the time on each plan. You can turn proration off for a single change.

title: Free trials
body: Subscriptions can start with a free trial of any length. The customer is charged at the end of the trial unless they cancel, and a reminder email can be sent a few days before.

title: Retrying failed subscription payments
body: If a renewal payment fails, it is retried automatically over the following weeks. You can choose how many retries happen and whether the subscription is canceled or paused afterwards.

title: Using test mode
body: Test mode lets you try payments without moving real money. Use the test card numbers from the documentation, and switch to live mode when you are ready to accept real payments.

title: Setting up webhooks
body: Webhooks send an event to your server when something happens, such as a successful payment or a new dispute. Each event is signed so you can confirm it came from us.
